Extension 3
.

There are constants internalizing normals, neutrals, and normal types.

\displaystyle{\mathbf{Prod}}:\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle A:\mathsf{NfTy}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle A:\mathsf{NfTy}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle A:\mathsf{NfTy}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle A:\mathsf{NfTy}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}(B:\mathsf{V}_{m}(A)\to{\mathsf{NfTy}_{m}})\to\mathsf{NfTy}_{m}

\displaystyle{\mathbf{Sum}}:(A:\mathsf{NfTy}_{m})(B:\mathsf{V}_{m}(A)\to\mathsf{NfTy}_{m})\to\mathsf{NfTy}_{m}

\displaystyle\mathbf{Id}:(A:\mathsf{NfTy}_{m})\to\mathsf{Nf}_{m}(A)\to\mathsf{Nf}_{m}(A)\to\mathsf{NfTy}_{m}

\displaystyle\mathbf{Bool}:\mathsf{NfTy}_{m}

\displaystyle\mathbf{Mod}_{\mu}:\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid\mathsf{NfTy}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid\mathsf{NfTy}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid\mathsf{NfTy}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid\mathsf{NfTy}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to\mathsf{NfTy}_{m}

\displaystyle\mathbf{lam}:\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle A:\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}\mathsf{Ty}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle A:\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}\mathsf{Ty}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle A:\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}\mathsf{Ty}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle A:\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}\mathsf{Ty}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}(B:{\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}\mathsf{Tm}_{m}(A)}\to{\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}\mathsf{Ty}_{m}})

\displaystyle\quad\to(\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle a:\mathsf{V}_{m}(A)$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle a:\mathsf{V}_{m}(A)$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle a:\mathsf{V}_{m}(A)$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a:\mathsf{V}_{m}(A)$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to{\mathsf{Nf}_{m}(B(a))})\to\mathsf{Nf}_{m}(\mathsf{Prod}(A,B))

\displaystyle\mathbf{app}:\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid A:\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}\mathsf{Ty}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid A:\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}\mathsf{Ty}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid A:\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}\mathsf{Ty}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid A:\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}\mathsf{Ty}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}(B:{\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}\mathsf{Tm}_{m}(A)}\to{\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}\mathsf{Ty}_{m}})

\displaystyle\quad\to\mathsf{Ne}_{m}(\mathsf{Prod}(A,B))\to\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid a:\mathsf{Nf}_{m}(A)$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid a:\mathsf{Nf}_{m}(A)$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid a:\mathsf{Nf}_{m}(A)$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid a:\mathsf{Nf}_{m}(A)$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to\mathsf{Ne}_{m}(B(a))

\displaystyle\mathbf{up}:\mathsf{Ne}_{m}(\mathsf{Bool})\to\mathsf{Nf}_{m}(\mathsf{Bool})

\displaystyle\mathbf{tt},\mathbf{ff}:\mathsf{Nf}_{m}(\mathsf{Bool})

\displaystyle\mathbf{if}:(A:\mathsf{V}_{m}(\mathsf{Bool})\to\mathsf{NfTy}_{m})

\displaystyle\quad\to\mathsf{Nf}_{m}(A(\mathsf{true}))\to\mathsf{Nf}_{m}(A(\mathsf{false}))\to(b:\mathsf{Ne}_{m}(\mathsf{Bool}))\to\mathsf{Ne}_{m}(A(b))

\displaystyle\mathbf{up}:(A:\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}\mathsf{Ty}_{m})(a_{0},a_{1}:\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}\mathsf{Tm}_{m}(A))

\displaystyle\quad\to\mathsf{Ne}_{m}(\mathsf{Id}(A,a_{0},a_{1}))\to\mathsf{Nf}_{m}(\mathsf{Id}(A,a_{0},a_{1}))

\displaystyle\mathbf{refl}{}:(A:\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}_{z}\mathsf{Ty}_{m}(z))(a:\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}_{z}\mathsf{Tm}_{m}(z,A(z)))\to\mathsf{Nf}_{m}(\mathsf{Id}(A,a,a))

\displaystyle\mathbf{J}:(A:\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}\mathsf{Ty}_{m})\,(B:(a_{0},a_{1}:\mathsf{V}_{m}(A))(p:\mathsf{V}_{m}(\mathsf{Id}(A,a_{0},a_{1})))\to\mathsf{NfTy}_{m})

\displaystyle\quad\to((a:\mathsf{V}_{m}(A))\to\mathsf{Nf}_{m}(B(a,a,\mathsf{refl}(a))))\,(a_{0},a_{1}:\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}_{z}\mathsf{Tm}_{m}(A))(p:\mathsf{Ne}_{m}(\mathsf{Id}(A,a_{0},a_{1})))

\displaystyle\quad\to\mathsf{Ne}_{m}(B(a_{0},a_{1},p))

(8)

In prose,
A:T
contains the code of a normal type
A.\mathsf{code}
as well as a proof-relevant predicate
on the elements of
A.\mathsf{code}
.

The last two fields ensure that (1) all elements tracked by this predicate can be assigned normal
forms, and (2) all neutrals lie within the predicate. We write
{\downarrow}_{A}
and
{\uparrow}_{A}
for

A.\mathsf{reify}
and
A.\mathsf{reflect}
. Of the two, the
\mathsf{reify}
is the crucial operation needed for
the normalization algorithm: it ensures that computable elements can be given normal
forms. Tait
[
Tai67
]
, however, has shown that the pair of operations is necessary to close
all type formers under just
\mathsf{reify}{}
.

We cannot simply define
\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m}=T
, as
T
does not satisfy the equation

z:\mathbf{syn}\vdash T=\mathsf{Ty}_{m}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}
. It does, however, satisfy this condition up to isomorphism:
under
z:\mathbf{syn}
, the types of
\mathsf{pred}{}
,
\mathsf{reflect}{}
, and
\mathsf{reify}{}
collapse to singletons,
while the type of
\mathsf{code}
collapses to
\mathsf{Ty}_{m}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}
by Extension
2
:

\displaystyle\alpha_{\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}}:\textstyle\prod_{z:\mathbf{syn}}T\cong\mathsf{Ty}_{m}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}

\displaystyle\alpha_{\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}}(z,A)=A.\mathsf{code}

Observe
\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{Ty}_{m},\alpha_{\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{Ty}_{m},\alpha_{\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}_{m},\alpha_{\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}_{m},\alpha_{\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}:\textstyle\sum_{A:\textnormal{$\fullmoon$}\mathsf{U}}\textstyle\prod_{z:\mathbf{syn}}A\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}\cong T
, so the

applies and we can define

Type connectives

It remains only to close
\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m},\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m},\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m},\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m},\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}
under all connectives. For mode-local connectives,
these constructions are very similar to those given by Sterling
[
Ste21
]

(Lemmas
22
,
23
,
24
,
and
25
). Modal types and dependent products, however, involve modalities
and thus are different than the other connectives
(Lemmas
20
and
21
).

Lemma 20
.

\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m},\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m},\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m},\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m},\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}
is closed under dependent products.

Proof 5.1
.

We must define two constants:

\displaystyle\mathsf{Prod}^{*}:\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid A:\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid A:\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid A:\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid \begin{cases}{\uparrow}\mathbf{letmod}_{\mu;\nu}(A,\lambda v.\ B\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\uparrow}v$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle{\uparrow}v$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\uparrow}v$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\uparrow}v$}\mathclose{}{)}}.\mathsf{code}{},\lambda x.\ {\downarrow}b\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\uparrow}x$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle{\uparrow}x$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\uparrow}x$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\uparrow}x$}\mathclose{}{)}},e)&\text{if }\mathsf{prf}=\iota_{1}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{mod}_{\nu}(e),\_$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{mod}_{\nu}(e),\_$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{mod}_{\nu}(e),\_$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{mod}_{\nu}(e),\_$}\mathclose{}{)}}\\

Lemma 22
.

\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m},\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m},\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m},\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m},\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}
is closed under dependent sums.

Proof 5.3
.

Fixing
A:\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m}
and
B:\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}(A)\to\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m}
. We must construct the following pair of
constants:

\displaystyle\mathsf{Sig}^{*}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle A,B$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle A,B$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle A,B$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle A,B$}\mathclose{}{)}}

\displaystyle:\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m}

\displaystyle\alpha_{\mathsf{Sig}^{*}}

\displaystyle:\mathsf{Tm}_{m}(\mathsf{Sig}^{*}(A,B))\cong\textstyle\sum_{a:\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}(A)}\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}(B(a))

Such that they lie over
\mathsf{Sig}
and
\alpha_{\mathsf{Sig}}
respectively.

We begin by applying realignment to the following:

\mathchoice{\mathopen{\mathchoice{\Big(}{\Big(}{\big(}{(}}\hbox{$\displaystyle\textstyle\sum_{a:A.\mathsf{pred}}B\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}.\mathsf{pred},\alpha_{\mathsf{Sig}(z)}$}\mathclose{\mathchoice{\Big)}{\Big)}{\big)}{)}}}{\mathopen{\mathchoice{\Big(}{\Big(}{\big(}{(}}\hbox{$\textstyle\textstyle\sum_{a:A.\mathsf{pred}}B\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}.\mathsf{pred},\alpha_{\mathsf{Sig}(z)}$}\mathclose{\mathchoice{\Big)}{\Big)}{\big)}{)}}}{\mathopen{\mathchoice{\Big(}{\Big(}{\big(}{(}}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\textstyle\sum_{a:A.\mathsf{pred}}B\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}.\mathsf{pred},\alpha_{\mathsf{Sig}(z)}$}\mathclose{\mathchoice{\Big)}{\Big)}{\big)}{)}}}{\mathopen{\mathchoice{\Big(}{\Big(}{\big(}{(}}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\textstyle\sum_{a:A.\mathsf{pred}}B\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}.\mathsf{pred},\alpha_{\mathsf{Sig}(z)}$}\mathclose{\mathchoice{\Big)}{\Big)}{\big)}{)}}}

This produces
\Psi:\mathsf{U}_{1}
and

\alpha_{\mathsf{Sig}^{*}}:\Psi\cong\textstyle\sum_{a:A.\mathsf{pred}}B\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle a$}\mathclose{}{)}}.\mathsf{pred}
such that under the assumption

z:\mathbf{syn}
the following holds:

\Psi=\mathsf{Tm}_{m}(\mathsf{Sig}(z,A,B))\qquad\alpha_{\mathsf{Sig}^{*}}=\alpha_{\mathsf{Sig}}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle z$}\mathclose{}{)}}

We now define
\mathsf{Sig}^{*}(A,B)

\displaystyle\mathsf{Sig}^{*}(A,B).\mathsf{code}={\mathbf{Sum}}(A.\mathsf{code},\lambda v.\ B.\mathsf{code}({\uparrow}_{A}v))

\displaystyle\mathsf{Sig}^{*}(A,B).\mathsf{pred}=\Psi

\displaystyle\mathsf{Sig}^{*}(A,B).\mathsf{reflect}=\lambda e.\ \alpha_{\mathsf{Sig}^{*}}^{-1}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{\langle}\hbox{$\displaystyle{\uparrow}_{A}(\mathbf{proj}_{0}(e)),{\uparrow}_{B({\uparrow}_{A}(\mathbf{proj}_{0}(e)))}(\mathbf{proj}_{1}(e))$}\mathclose{}{\rangle}}{\mathopen{}{\langle}\hbox{$\textstyle{\uparrow}_{A}(\mathbf{proj}_{0}(e)),{\uparrow}_{B({\uparrow}_{A}(\mathbf{proj}_{0}(e)))}(\mathbf{proj}_{1}(e))$}\mathclose{}{\rangle}}{\mathopen{}{\langle}\hbox{$\scriptstyle{\uparrow}_{A}(\mathbf{proj}_{0}(e)),{\uparrow}_{B({\uparrow}_{A}(\mathbf{proj}_{0}(e)))}(\mathbf{proj}_{1}(e))$}\mathclose{}{\rangle}}{\mathopen{}{\langle}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle{\uparrow}_{A}(\mathbf{proj}_{0}(e)),{\uparrow}_{B({\uparrow}_{A}(\mathbf{proj}_{0}(e)))}(\mathbf{proj}_{1}(e))$}\mathclose{}{\rangle}}

\displaystyle\mathsf{Sig}^{*}(A,B).\mathsf{reify}=\lambda p.\ \mathbf{pair}({\downarrow}_{A}(\alpha_{\mathsf{Sig}^{*}}p.0),{\downarrow}_{B(\alpha_{\mathsf{Sig}^{*}}p.0)}(\alpha_{\mathsf{Sig}^{*}}p.1))

The fact that
{\downarrow}

MTT
. We show the calculations for
{\uparrow}
. Fix

:

such
that
\alpha\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\llbracket\Gamma\rrbracket\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\llbracket\Gamma\rrbracket\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\llbracket\Gamma\rrbracket\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\llbracket\Gamma\rrbracket\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}=\mathsf{id}:\mathbf{i}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{[}\hbox{$\displaystyle m$}\mathclose{}{]}}{\mathopen{}{[}\hbox{$\textstyle m$}\mathclose{}{]}}{\mathopen{}{[}\hbox{$\scriptstyle m$}\mathclose{}{]}}{\mathopen{}{[}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle m$}\mathclose{}{]}}^{*}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathbf{y}(\Gamma)$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathbf{y}(\Gamma)$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathbf{y}(\Gamma)$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathbf{y}(\Gamma)$}\mathclose{}{)}}_{\Gamma}
:
pushing
\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}
along the top of the diagram would yield a normal form (an element of

\pi_{1}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{Nf}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{Nf}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{Nf}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{Nf}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}
) which decodes to
M
by Yoneda. Modulo technical details,
\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}
is
produced by using
{\uparrow}
to convert variables for each element of
\Gamma
into elements of

\pi_{1}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\llbracket\Gamma\rrbracket$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\llbracket\Gamma\rrbracket$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\llbracket\Gamma\rrbracket$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\llbracket\Gamma\rrbracket$}\mathclose{}{)}}
.

Lemma 28
.

For any
\Gamma\ \mathsf{cx}{}\mathop{@}m
there exists
\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}:\pi_{1}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\llbracket\Gamma\rrbracket$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\llbracket\Gamma\rrbracket$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\llbracket\Gamma\rrbracket$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\llbracket\Gamma\rrbracket$}\mathclose{}{)}}_{\Gamma}
lying
over
\mathsf{id}:\mathbf{i}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{[}\hbox{$\displaystyle m$}\mathclose{}{]}}{\mathopen{}{[}\hbox{$\textstyle m$}\mathclose{}{]}}{\mathopen{}{[}\hbox{$\scriptstyle m$}\mathclose{}{]}}{\mathopen{}{[}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle m$}\mathclose{}{]}}^{*}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathbf{y}(\Gamma)$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathbf{y}(\Gamma)$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathbf{y}(\Gamma)$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathbf{y}(\Gamma)$}\mathclose{}{)}}
.

Proof 6.2
.

This proof proceeds by induction on
\Gamma
.

Case:

\Gamma=\mathbf{1}

Here
\llbracket\Gamma\rrbracket
is terminal, so
\mathsf{atoms}_{\mathbf{1}}
is its unique element. The requirement
that
\mathsf{atoms}_{\mathbf{1}}
lie over
\mathsf{id}
is then tautological.

Case:

\Gamma=\Delta.\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid A$}\mathclose{}{)}}

In this case, we note that

\llbracket\Gamma\rrbracket=\llbracket\Delta\rrbracket\times_{\mathcal{G}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}}\mathcal{G}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}
and, since pullback are computed pointwise, it suffices to
construct element of
\pi_{1}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\llbracket\Delta\rrbracket_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\llbracket\Delta\rrbracket_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\llbracket\Delta\rrbracket_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\llbracket\Delta\rrbracket_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}
and

\pi_{1}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathcal{G}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathcal{G}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathcal{G}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathcal{G}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}
separately which agree on

\pi_{1}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathcal{G}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathcal{G}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathcal{G}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathcal{G}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{n}$}\mathclose{}{)}}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}
.

First, we reindex
\mathsf{atoms}_{\Delta}
by
\Gamma\vdash{\uparrow}:\Delta{}\mathop{@}m
to
obtain
\delta\in\llbracket\Delta\rrbracket_{\Gamma}
. Next, using the element

\mathbf{v}_{0}\in\mathcal{G}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{Ne}_{n}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{Ne}_{n}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{Ne}_{n}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{Ne}_{n}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}_{\Gamma}
we define

\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}=\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\delta,{\uparrow}_{A}\mathbf{v}_{0}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\delta,{\uparrow}_{A}\mathbf{v}_{0}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\delta,{\uparrow}_{A}\mathbf{v}_{0}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\delta,{\uparrow}_{A}\mathbf{v}_{0}$}\mathclose{}{)}}
. The check that this lies over
\mathsf{id}

follows from the fact that (1)
\delta
lies over
{\uparrow}
, (2)
{\uparrow}_{A}\mathbf{v}_{0}
lies over

\mathbf{v}_{0}
and (3) that
{{\uparrow}}.{\mathbf{v}_{0}}=\mathsf{id}
.

Case:

\Gamma=\Delta.\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}

We define
\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}=\mathcal{G}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{)}}_{!}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Delta}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Delta}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Delta}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Delta}$}\mathclose{}{)}}
.
The check that this lies over
\mathsf{id}
amounts to the equation in syntax that

\mathsf{id}{}.\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}=\mathsf{id}
.

Remark 29
.

\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}
is analogous to the initial environment used in classical NbE proofs to kick off
normalization. Abel
[
Abe13
]
, for instance, denotes the environment
\uparrow^{\Gamma}
.

Combining Lemma
28
with the argument above, we conclude that for term

\Gamma\vdash M:A{}\mathop{@}m
, there exists
\Gamma\vdash^{\!\!\raisebox{0.0pt}{\tiny$\mathsf{nf}$}}u:A{}\mathop{@}m
such that
\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}=M
. Moreover, because we
have consistently worked with equivalences class of terms, this function automatically respects
definitional equality. Summarizing:

Theorem 30
.

There is a function
\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle-,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle-,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle-,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle-,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}
sending terms of type
\Gamma\vdash A{}\mathop{@}{m}
to normal forms such that

(1)

If
\Gamma\vdash M:A{}\mathop{@}m
then
\Gamma\vdash\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}=M:A{}\mathop{@}m
.

(2)

If
\Gamma\vdash M=N:A{}\mathop{@}m
then
\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}=\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}
.

By again pushing

along the top of this diagram, we obtain a normalization function

Theorem 31
.

There is a function
\mathbf{nfty}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle-$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle-$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle-$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle-$}\mathclose{}{)}}
sending types to normal types such that

(1)

If
\Gamma\vdash A{}\mathop{@}{m}
then
\Gamma\vdash\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathbf{nfty}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathbf{nfty}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathbf{nfty}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathbf{nfty}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}=A{}\mathop{@}{m}
.

(2)

If
\Gamma\vdash A=B{}\mathop{@}{m}
then
\mathbf{nfty}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}=\mathbf{nfty}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle B$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle B$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle B$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle B$}\mathclose{}{)}}
.

6.2.
Corollaries of normalization

A number of important theorems follow as corollaries of
Theorems
30
and
31
. For
instance, we can reduce the decidability of conversion to the decidability of normal forms.

Corollary 32
.

(1)

\Gamma\vdash M=N:A{}\mathop{@}m
iff
\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}=\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}
.

(2)

\Gamma\vdash A=B{}\mathop{@}{m}
iff
\mathbf{nfty}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{)}}=\mathbf{nfty}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle B$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle B$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle B$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle B$}\mathclose{}{)}}
.

Proof 6.3
.

We show only the proof for this first claim. The ‘only if’ direction is established by the second
point of Theorem
30
. Suppose instead

\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}=\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}
, so

\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}=\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle N,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}
. By the first point of
Theorem
30
,
\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}=M
and

\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M,A$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{|}}=N
, so the conclusion follows.

A priori, however, a given term could have multiple normal forms which complicates further
analysis. We therefore strengthen Theorem
30
with the following:

Theorem 33

(Tightness)
.

(1)

If
\Gamma\vdash^{\!\!\raisebox{0.0pt}{\tiny$\mathsf{nf}$}}u:A{}\mathop{@}m
, then
\mathbf{nf}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}},A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}},A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}},A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}},A$}\mathclose{}{)}}=u
.

(2)

If
\Gamma\vdash^{\!\!\raisebox{0.0pt}{\tiny$\mathsf{nf}$}}\tau{}\mathop{@}m
, then
\mathbf{nfty}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}=\tau
.

Proof 6.4
.

Recall that Theorems
5
and
26
induce a
function
\llbracket-\rrbracket
sending a piece of syntax to its interpretation in the normalization
model. Furthermore, recall the
\Gamma
-element
\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}:\llbracket\Gamma\rrbracket

constructed in Lemma
28
.

We begin by strengthening the statement to make it more amenable to induction:

(1)

If
\Gamma\vdash^{\!\!\raisebox{0.0pt}{\tiny$\mathsf{ne}$}}e:A{}\mathop{@}m
, then

\llbracket\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle M$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle M$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle M$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle M$}\mathclose{}{|}}\rrbracket(\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma})={\uparrow}_{\llbracket A\rrbracket(\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma})}e

(2)

If
\Gamma\vdash^{\!\!\raisebox{0.0pt}{\tiny$\mathsf{nf}$}}u:A{}\mathop{@}m
, then

{\downarrow}_{\llbracket A\rrbracket(\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma})}\llbracket\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle u$}\mathclose{}{|}}\rrbracket(\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma})=u
.

(3)

If
\Gamma\vdash^{\!\!\raisebox{0.0pt}{\tiny$\mathsf{nf}$}}\tau{}\mathop{@}m
, then
{\llbracket\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle A$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle A$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle A$}\mathclose{}{|}}\rrbracket.\mathsf{code}(\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma})}=\tau
.

Here we have identified a code
u
(resp.
e
) as an
\Gamma
-element of
\mathsf{Nf}_{A}

(resp.
\mathsf{Ne}_{A}
). All three follow straightforwardly from mutual induction and the relevant
definitions. For instance, if we consider
\Gamma\vdash^{\!\!\raisebox{0.0pt}{\tiny$\mathsf{nf}$}}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to\sigma{}\mathop{@}m
, we calculate as
follows:

\displaystyle\llbracket\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to\sigma$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to\sigma$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to\sigma$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to\sigma$}\mathclose{}{|}}\rrbracket.\mathsf{code}(\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma})

\displaystyle={\llbracket\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\sigma$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\sigma$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\sigma$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\sigma$}\mathclose{}{|}}\rrbracket.\mathsf{code}(\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma})}

\displaystyle=\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid{\llbracket\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}\rrbracket}.\mathsf{code}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid{\llbracket\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}\rrbracket}.\mathsf{code}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid{\llbracket\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}\rrbracket}.\mathsf{code}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\ \displaystyle=\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid{\llbracket\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}\rrbracket}.\mathsf{code}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid{\llbracket\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}\rrbracket}.\mathsf{code}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid{\llbracket\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\tau$}\mathclose{}{|}}\rrbracket}.\mathsf{code}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{atoms}_{\Gamma}$}\mathclose{}{)}}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\ A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid A$}\mathclose{}{)}}})

\displaystyle=\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid\tau$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to\sigma

In order to carry out this calculation, we took advantage of not only the definition of dependent
products in the gluing model, but also the interpretation of HOAS and
\mathsf{atoms}
.

Corollary 34
.

Normalization is an isomorphism between equivalence classes of terms (resp. types) and normal
forms (resp. normal types).

Proof 6.5
.

Corollary
32
already shows that normalization is injective and
Theorem
33
provides a section.

These results imply the injectivity of type constructors, an essential property for implementation.

Corollary 35
.

If
\Gamma\vdash A_{0}\to B_{0}=A_{1}\to B_{1}{}\mathop{@}{m}
then
\Gamma\vdash A_{0}=A_{1}{}\mathop{@}{m}
and

\Gamma.\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{id}\mid A_{0}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{id}\mid A_{0}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{id}\mid A_{0}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{id}\mid A_{0}$}\mathclose{}{)}}\vdash B_{0}=B_{1}{}\mathop{@}{m}
.

Proof 6.6
.

Set
\tau_{i}=\mathbf{nfty}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle A_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle A_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle A_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle A_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}
and
\sigma_{i}=\mathbf{nfty}_{\Gamma.\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{id}\mid A_{0}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{id}\mid A_{0}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{id}\mid A_{0}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{id}\mid A_{0}$}\mathclose{}{)}}}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle B_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle B_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle B_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle B_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}
. Unfolding definitions shows that

\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to\sigma_{i}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to\sigma_{i}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to\sigma_{i}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to\sigma_{i}$}\mathclose{}{|}}=\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{|}}\to\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\displaystyle\sigma_{i}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\textstyle\sigma_{i}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\sigma_{i}$}\mathclose{}{|}}{\mathopen{}{|}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\sigma_{i}$}\mathclose{}{|}}=A_{i}\to B_{i}
. By
Corollary
34
,

\mathbf{nfty}_{\Gamma}\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle A_{i}\to B_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle A_{i}\to B_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle A_{i}\to B_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle A_{i}\to B_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}=\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid\tau_{i}$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to\sigma_{i}
.

Next, we recall that
\Gamma\vdash A_{0}\to B_{0}=A_{1}\to B_{1}{}\mathop{@}{m}
by assumption, so

\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid\tau_{0}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid\tau_{0}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid\tau_{0}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid\tau_{0}$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to\sigma_{0}=\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid\tau_{1}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid\tau_{1}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid\tau_{1}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid\tau_{1}$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to\sigma_{1}
. As an operation on normal forms, however,

\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid-$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid-$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid-$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid-$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to-
is clearly injective, so
\tau_{0}=\tau_{1}
and
\sigma_{0}=\sigma_{1}
. The result
now follows from Corollary
32
.

In light of Corollary
32
, to decide the equality of terms and types, it suffices to
argue that one may decide the equality of neutral and normal forms along with normal types. For this
purpose, we adapt the bidirectional algorithm given by Altenkirch and
Kaposi
[
AK17
]
. This argument goes through essentially without alteration, except
that since certain constructors are annotated with 1- and 2-cells from
\mathcal{M}
, we require a
decision procedure for objects in the mode theory. Note that this procedure uses e.g.,
Corollary
35
, which is why we have delayed its statement till now.

Corollary 36
.

If
\mathcal{M}
is decidable, type checking is decidable.

Finally, Gratzer et al.
[
GKNB20a
]
show canonicity for
MTT
extended with the equality

\mathbf{1}.\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}=\mathbf{1}
. Normalization provides a (heavy-handed) proof of canonicity without this
equation by scrutinizing the definition of normal forms:

Corollary 37
.

If
\mathbf{1}.\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}\vdash M:\mathsf{bool}{}\mathop{@}m
then
M\in\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{tt},\mathsf{ff}$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{tt},\mathsf{ff}$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{tt},\mathsf{ff}$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{tt},\mathsf{ff}$}\mathclose{}{\}}}
.

7.
Extending
MTT
with crisp identity induction

To demonstrate the flexibility of the normalization argument given in

5
and
6

MTT

Recall that, intuitively, a modality in
MTT
corresponds to a right adjoint. This intuition is
supported by the fact that
MTT
modalities commute with products. In an extensional version of

MTT

an equivalence:

\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid x,y:A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid x,y:A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid x,y:A$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid x,y:A$}\mathclose{}{)}}\to\mathsf{Id}_{\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{\langle}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid A$}\mathclose{}{\rangle}}{\mathopen{}{\langle}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid A$}\mathclose{}{\rangle}}{\mathopen{}{\langle}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid A$}\mathclose{}{\rangle}}{\mathopen{}{\langle}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid A$}\mathclose{}{\rangle}}}(\mathsf{mod}_{\mu}(x),\mathsf{mod}_{\mu}(y))\to\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{\langle}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu\mid\mathsf{Id}_{A}(x,y)$}\mathclose{}{\rangle}}{\mathopen{}{\langle}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu\mid\mathsf{Id}_{A}(x,y)$}\mathclose{}{\rangle}}{\mathopen{}{\langle}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu\mid\mathsf{Id}_{A}(x,y)$}\mathclose{}{\rangle}}{\mathopen{}{\langle}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu\mid\mathsf{Id}_{A}(x,y)$}\mathclose{}{\rangle}}

(11)

In

Unfolding the interpretation of Equation
11
, we observe that an inverse to

. As function

, there must be no inverse to

definable within
MTT
.

In light of Theorem
38
, we refer to the existence of an inverse to
Equation
11
as

. Modal extensionality is useful in
practice. In incarnations of guarded recursion within
MTT
, for instance, some version of modal
extensionality is required to prove any equalities involving guarded
types
[
GKNB21
,
GB22
]
. It is therefore worth investigating whether
modal extensionality is compatible with both normalization and canonicity.
7
7

7

Like function
extensionality, it is straightforward to maintain
either
normalization or canonicity in the
presence of modal extensionality. Ensuring for both simultaneously is far more difficult.

In work by Shulman
[
Shu18
]
and Gratzer
[
GKNB21
]
,
crisp

induction principles are a variation of the induction principles for types such as
\mathsf{bool}
or

\mathsf{Id}_{A}(a_{0},a_{1})
which allow the scrutinee of the induction to occur beneath a modality. Crisp
induction principles are derivable in
MTT
if the modality has an internal right
adjoint
[
GKNB21
]
, but they are justified in other situations. In particular,
crisp induction for identity types is validated if and only if modal extensionality holds. In
contrast to modal extensionality, however, it is straightforward to directly adapt the proofs of
normalization and canonicity to account for crisp identity induction principles:

Lemma 39
.

\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m},\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m},\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m},\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mathsf{Ty}^{*}_{m},\mathsf{Tm}^{*}_{m}$}\mathclose{}{)}}

Proof 7.2
.

This argument is similar to Lemma

8.
Related work

We have built on top of a long line of research systematically structuring logical relations as gluing
models
[
MS93
,
AHS95
,
Str98
,
Fio02
,
Shu15
,
AK17
,
KHS19
,
Coq19
,
SA21
,
Ste21
]
.
In particular, Altenkirch et al.
[
AHS95
]
and Fiore
[
Fio02
]
recast NbE
into the construction of a gluing model in which types are triples

\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\displaystyle A,{\downarrow},{\uparrow}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\textstyle A,{\downarrow},{\uparrow}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptstyle A,{\downarrow},{\uparrow}$}\mathclose{}{)}}{\mathopen{}{(}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle A,{\downarrow},{\uparrow}$}\mathclose{}{)}}
. Generalizing from this work to dependent type theory has proven a
considerable challenge
[
AK16
]
. The final ingredient for Martin-Löf type theory
was provided by Coquand
[
Coq19
]
: a construction of a universe in this gluing model similar to
that of Shulman
[
Shu15
]
.

Gluing for modal type theory

Gratzer et al.
[
GSB19a
]
gave a classical normalization-by-evaluation proof for a
Fitch-style type theory. The complexity of this proof, however, makes it intractable to extend to a
general modal type theory like
MTT
. Unfortunately, extending gluing techniques to modal type
theories has proven challenging. In particular, Gratzer et al.
[
GKNB20a
]
used gluing to
prove canonicity for
MTT
, but they were forced to add an additional equality to
MTT

(
\mathbf{1}.\mathchoice{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\displaystyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\textstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\scriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}{\mathopen{}{\{}\hbox{$\scriptscriptstyle\mu$}\mathclose{}{\}}}=\mathbf{1}
) to tame the construction of the gluing model. The challenge lies in
fitting the glued category of contexts into a CwF-style model of type theory; the natural definition
of glued types and terms fails to admit modalities. While there have been some attempts to
systematize the construction of glued CwFs
[
KHS19
]
, they do not apply to
MTT
.

Recently, Hu and Pientka
[
HP22
]
gave a proof of normalization for a simply-typed Fitch-style
type theory (Kripke-style in their parlance) with one modality. They give two separate proofs of
normalization; one through both an untyped PER model similar to Gratzer et al.
[
GSB19a
]

and one using a gluing model. Their gluing proof is closely related to the argument above. For
instance, their theory of unified substitutions and modal transformations corresponds to a
specialization of
MTT
’s substitution calculus to one modality and, accordingly, their category of
renamings offers a strict presentation of the category of renamings described above. Their proof,
however, is done using external constructions on the gluing category which may make it difficult to
scale to either multiple modalities or dependent types.

Synthetic Tait computability

The introduction of representable map categories
[
Uem19
]
and
LCCCs
[
GS20
]
for modeling the syntax of (non-modal) type theory offered an
alternative approach. Crucially, they show that syntax can be given a universal property among
structured categories with better behavior than CwFs. Sterling and
collaborators
[
SH21
,
SA21
,
Ste21
]
have built on this idea and
introduced synthetic Tait computability to prove syntactic metatheorems via gluing together LCCCs
rather than CwFs. Unlike other approaches to gluing, STC generalizes well to a multimodal setting
and by extending STC to MSTC normalization for
MTT
becomes tractable.

MTT
as a metalanguage

In a parallel line of work, Bocquet et al.
[
BKS21
]
have also used
MTT
as a
metalanguage in the construction of models of type theory. They, however, do not work with a modal
object type theory and instead use
MTT
to internalize a functor
F
rather than working
internally to
\mathbf{Gl}(F)
. As a result, while both proofs use
MTT
modalities, the modalities used by
op. cit. are encoded in our proof by fibered lex monads (
\fullmoon
,
\newmoon
) which prove easier to
manipulate.

9.
Conclusions and future work

We prove normalization for
MTT
(Theorem
30
) and thereby reduce
the decidability of conversion and type checking to the decidability of equality of the underlying
mode theory (Corollaries
32
and
36
). In
addition, we deduce a number of corollaries from normalization itself, including the injectivity of
type constructors and canonicity (Corollaries
35
and

37
).

By working constructively, we have obtained an effective procedure for normalization. This, along
with our results on type checking, open the door to a theoretically-sound implementation of
MTT

generic in the mode theory. In the future, we intend to develop a bidirectional syntax for
MTT

and implement it. Stassen et al.
[
SGB22
]
have made promising initial steps in this
direction for
poset-enriched
mode theories.
